h: Purchasing a Permanent Dwelling for Holiness

p: "וַיָּבֹא יַעֲקֹב שָׁלֵם עִיר שְׁכֶם וְגוֹמֵר וַיִּקֶן אֶת חֶלְקַת הַשָּׂדֶה וְגוֹמֵר" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לג, יח–יט).
— And Jacob came whole to the city of Shechem... and he bought the parcel of ground, etc. (Genesis 33:18–19).
וְאִיתָא בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה עַל זֶה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה עט, ז):
— And it is taught in Midrash Rabbah on this (Bereishit Rabbah 79:7):
"זֶה אֶחָד מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת שֶׁאֵין אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם יְכוֹלִין לְהוֹנוֹת אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לוֹמַר 'גְּזוּלִים הֵן בְּיֶדְכֶם':
— "This is one of the three places where the nations of the world cannot taunt Israel, saying: 'They are stolen in your hand':
מְעָרַת הַמַּכְפֵּלָה, וּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, וּקְבוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף – שֶׁהוּא שְׁכֶם – שֶׁקָּנוּ אוֹתָם בְּדָמִים".
— the Cave of Machpelah, the Temple Mount, and the burial place of Joseph—which is Shechem—which they purchased with full money."

p: וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלִּקְבּוֹעַ מְקוֹם קְדוּשָּׁה צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בְּכֶסֶף וּבִמְחִיר,
— Meaning that to establish a permanent sanctuary of holiness on earth requires actual silver and purchase-price,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, קכח עַמּוּד א):
— as written in the holy Zohar (Part II, 128a):
"אִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָא דְּקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא דְּקַיְימָא בְּעוֹבָדָא וְכוּלֵי, לְאַמְשָׁכָא עֲלֵיהּ רוּחַ דְּקֻדְשָׁא בַּאֲגַר שְׁלִים".
— "The spiritual exertion for the Holy One, blessed be He, which exists in physical deed... to draw down upon oneself the Holy Spirit must be through full payment."
וְכָאן שֶׁבָּא לִשְׁכֶם, וּכְתִיב: "וַיִּחַן אֶת פְּנֵי הָעִיר", שֶׁאָמְרוּ שֶׁקָּבַע תְּחוּמִין –
— And here, when Jacob arrived at Shechem, where it is written: "and he encamped before the city," which the Sages expounded as establishing techumin—
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁקָּבַע הַמָּקוֹם בִּקְדוּשָּׁה מֵעֵין קְדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת,
— meaning he consecrated that physical territory with holiness reflecting the sanctity of Shabbat,
וְזֶה הָיָה בִּשְׁכֶם בְּרֵאשִׁית כְּנִיסָתוֹ לָאָרֶץ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה,
— and this occurred at Shechem at the very threshold of his entry into the Holy Land,
וְעַל כֵּן קָנָה הַמָּקוֹם בַּאֲגַר שְׁלִים.
— wherefore he purchased the territory with full and complete payment.

paragraphs.text: Zohar Terumah 6:35: “True, it is written, ‘Come ye, buy wine and milk without money and without price’ (Isa. 55, 1), and this in reference to work on behalf of the Holy One. But this only indicates that, whereas knowledge of the Holy One and of His Torah can be acquired without price or fee, the doing of good works for the sake of Heaven requires sacrifice and must be ‘paid for’ with full price; otherwise the doer is not worthy to draw down unto himself the spirit of holiness from above.”

h: Refining the Three Failings of Shechem

p: וְהָעִנְיָן, עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (סַנְהֶדְרִין קב עַמּוּד א):
— And the inner reason is based on Sanhedrin (102a):
דִּשְׁכֶם מָקוֹם מְזוּמָּן לְפוּרְעָנוּת:
— that Shechem was a place historically primed for tragedy:
בִּשְׁכֶם עִנּוּ אֶת דִּינָה, בִּשְׁכֶם מָכְרוּ אֶת יוֹסֵף, בִּשְׁכֶם נֶחְלְקָה מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד.
— in Shechem Dinah was violated, in Shechem the brothers sold Joseph, and in Shechem the kingdom of the House of David was torn asunder.
וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בָּא לְתַקֵּן אֶת הַמָּקוֹם בִּקְדוּשַׁת הָאָרֶץ,
— And our father Jacob, peace be upon him, came to sanctify that place with the sanctity of the Land,
לְהַשְׁרִישׁ בָּהּ קְדוּשַׁת הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת שֶׁהֵם הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁל חַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם;
— rooting within it the holiness of the three Patriarchs who are the foundation of eternal life;
וּמִמֵּילָא בְּהֶכְרֵחַ לְתַקֵּן שְׁלֹשָׁה הַפְּגָמִים: הַקִּנְאָה, הַתַּאֲוָה, וְהַכָּבוֹד,
— which perforce required rectifying the three primordial flaws of envy, lust, and honor,
שֶׁהֵם מְנַגְּדִים לִקְדוּשַּׁת שְׁלֹשָׁה הָאָבוֹת וְהֵם מוֹצִיאִין אֶת הָאָדָם מֵחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם.
— which combat the Patriarchal attributes and drive man out of eternal life.
וּבִשְׁכֶם הָיָה בְּיִחוּד הַמָּקוֹם הַמּוּכָן לִשְׁלֹשָׁה פְּגָמִים אֵלּוּ:
— And Shechem was uniquely the geographical focus for these three blemishes:
עִנּוּ אֶת דִּינָה – פְּגַם הַתַּאֲוָה;
— the violation of Dinah—the blemish of lust;
וּמָכְרוּ אֶת יוֹסֵף בָּא מִקִּנְאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיְקַנְאוּ בוֹ אֶחָיו" (בְּרֵאשִׁית לז, יא);
— the selling of Joseph stemmed from envy, as it is written: "and his brothers envied him";
וְגַם אִיתָא (מַכּוֹת י עַמּוּד א): בִּשְׁכֶם נַמֵּי שְׁכִיחֵי רוֹצְחִים, דִּכְתִיב: "דֶּרֶךְ יְרַצְּחוּ שֶׁכְמָה" (הוֹשֵׁעַ ו, ט),
— and in Makkot (10a): murderers were rampant in Shechem, as it is said: "as troops of robbers wait for a man, so the company of priests murder in the way to Shechem",
וְכַעַס וּרְצִיחָה בָּא מִפְּגַם הַקִּנְאָה;
— and anger and murder emerge directly from envy;
וְנֶחְלְקָה מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד מִצַּד פְּגַם הַכָּבוֹד,
— and the fracturing of the Davidic dynasty occurred through the pursuit of honor:
כִּי רְחַבְעָם לֹא רָצָה לִפְגּוֹם בִּכְבוֹדוֹ, לוֹמַר: "קָטָנִּי עָבָה מִמָּתְנֵי אָבִי" (מְלָכִים א יב, י),
— for Rehoboam refused to compromise his personal prestige, boasting: "my little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins",
וּבְיָרָבְעָם אִיתָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין קא עַמּוּד ב): "גַּסּוּת הָרוּחַ שֶׁהָיָה בוֹ בְּיָרָבְעָם טְרָדַתּוּ מִן הָעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי", עַיֵּין שָׁם.
— and regarding Jeroboam it is taught in Sanhedrin (101b): "The haughtiness of spirit within Jeroboam drove him from the world," see there.

p: וְהֲגַם שֶׁכָּל הַקִּלְקוּלִים הָיוּ אַחַר שֶׁקָּנָה יַעֲקֹב שְׁכֶם וְקָבַע בּוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה,
— And even though all these tragic failures erupted chronologically after Jacob purchased Shechem and consecrated it,
אָמְנָם פָּעַל בָּזֶה יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לְהַכְנִיעָם,
— nonetheless, through that purchase Jacob implanted the latent power to subdue them,
שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בְּכֹחַ נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהִתְגַּבֵּר וּלְהִתְעַצֵּם בִּכְדֵי לְהַגִּיעַ לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַחַיִּים.
— empowering Jewish souls throughout history to overcome these drives and cleave unto the Source of Life.
וְזֶה עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ קְדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת,
— And this is mediated through the sanctity of Shabbat,
שֶׁזּוֹכִין לִקְדוּשַׁת הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת בִּקְדוּשַׁת שָׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת שַׁבָּת,
— wherein we merit the holiness of the three Patriarchs across the three Shabbat meals,
וְנִכְנָעִים שְׁלֹשָׁה הַפְּגָמִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל.
— and these three blemishes are decisively subdued.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Beit Yaakov, Vayishlach §45, paragraph 3: “The place of Shechem likewise involved such great concealment and severe judgment that human apprehension could not grasp how God’s providence for good was present there. When our father Jacob wished to acquire a portion there, he had to expend his money and give one hundred kesitah. … In truth, Jacob felt no anguish over this loss, since he had already attained his completeness. He trusted God that all the losses Israel suffers because of severe judgment, such as at Shechem and similar places, are only like sowing: a person sows a seed in the earth and the seed is lost, yet he is confident that through it much more will grow than he sowed. Does a person sow a kor except to bring in many kor from it? So too, through the suffering that Israel endures in this world, they will gain in the future an outpouring of goodness from God beyond measure and estimation.”

: “The place of Shechem likewise involved such great concealment and severe judgment that human apprehension could not grasp how God’s providence for good was present there. When our father Jacob wished to acquire a portion there, he had to expend his money and give one hundred kesitah. … In truth, Jacob felt no anguish over this loss, since he had already attained his completeness. He trusted God that all the losses Israel suffers because of severe judgment, such as at Shechem and similar places, are only like sowing: a person sows a seed in the earth and the seed is lost, yet he is confident that through it much more will grow than he sowed. Does a person sow a kor except to bring in many kor from it? So too, through the suffering that Israel endures in this world, they will gain in the future an outpouring of goodness from God beyond measure and estimation.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Rav Tzadok explains why Jacob’s purchase remained effective even though Shechem’s later history still contained grave failures: it planted a power that Israel would realize afterward. Beit Yaakov develops the same delay through the image of sowing. The costly acquisition is a seed whose fruit is initially concealed. This clarifies how present expenditure and subsequent suffering can coexist with the purchase’s enduring spiritual achievement.

p: וְזָכַר מְעָרַת הַמַּכְפֵּלָה וּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁקְּנָאוּם בְּדָמִים:
— And the Midrash coupled Shechem with the Cave of Machpelah and the Temple Mount which were purchased with full payment:
דְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, שֶׁהוּא לַעֲשׂוֹת מָקוֹם לַה', צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בַּאֲגַר שְׁלִים וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם);
— for the Temple, which establishes an earthly dwelling for Hashem, must be acquired through full compensation as the Zohar states;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בַּעֲשִׂיַּת הַמִּשְׁכָּן, שֶׁצִּוָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ: "מֵאֵת כָּל אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר יִדְּבֶנּוּ לִבּוֹ תִּקְחוּ אֶת תְּרוּמָתִי" (שְׁמוֹת כה, ב) –
— as was with the Tabernacle, Hashem commanding: "of every man whose heart makes him willing you shall take My offering"—
וּבְוַדַּאי לֹא נֶחְסַר לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב,
— for the Holy One certainly does not lack gold or silver,
רַק לִקְבּוֹעַ מְקוֹם קְדוּשָּׁה צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בִּמְחִיר וְנִדְבוֹת לֵב, וּמִזֶּה נַעֲשָׂה הַמִּשְׁכָּן.
— rather, rooting a place of holiness on earth requires human sacrifice, purchase-price, and devotion of heart, from which the Sanctuary is built.
וְכֵן אָמַר דָּוִד לַאֲרַוְנָה כְּשֶׁקָּנָה מְקוֹם הַמִּקְדָּשׁ: "לֹא, כִּי קָנוֹ אֶקְנֶה מֵאוֹתְךָ בִּמְחִיר וְגוֹמֵר" (שְׁמוּאֵל ב כד, כד).

— And so King David insisted to Araunah when acquiring the Temple Mount: "No, but I will surely buy it of you at a price, neither will I offer burnt-offerings unto Hashem my God of that which costs me nothing."

paragraphs.text: Zohar Terumah 6:35: “True, it is written, ‘Come ye, buy wine and milk without money and without price’ (Isa. 55, 1), and this in reference to work on behalf of the Holy One. But this only indicates that, whereas knowledge of the Holy One and of His Torah can be acquired without price or fee, the doing of good works for the sake of Heaven requires sacrifice and must be ‘paid for’ with full price; otherwise the doer is not worthy to draw down unto himself the spirit of holiness from above.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Terumah 6:37: “But the spirit of holiness is not so: it demands a full price and strenuous effort, purification of one’s self and one’s dwelling, devotion of heart and soul; and even so one will be lucky to win it to take up its abode with him. Therefore one must beware and walk straitly according to the paths and ways of righteousness, turning neither to the right hand nor to the left; for otherwise, even if it had entered into a man, it will straightway depart from him, and thereafter it will indeed be passing hard to recall it again.”

p: וּמְעָרַת הַמַּכְפֵּלָה, שֶׁאָז לֹא נִתְקַדֵּשׁ עֲדַיִן מְקוֹם הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
— And regarding the Cave of Machpelah: in that era before the Temple Mount was consecrated,
הָיָה הַשְׁרָאַת הַשְּׁכִינָה בִּמְקוֹם קְבוּרַת הַצַּדִּיקִים,
— the dwelling of the Shechinah rested upon the burial site of the righteous;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ (סוֹטָה לד עַמּוּד ב) שֶׁפֵּירַשׁ כָּלֵב מֵעֲצַת מְרַגְּלִים וְהָלַךְ וְנִשְׁתַּטַּח עַל קִבְרֵי אָבוֹת, עַיֵּין שָׁם,
— as we find regarding Caleb who separated from the spies and prostrated himself upon the graves of the Patriarchs in Hebron (Sotah 34b),
דְּשָׁם הָיָה מָקוֹם מְקוּדָּשׁ לִתְפִלָּה.
— because that was the consecrated gateway for prayer.
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁרָאָה אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם דְּשָׁם הָיָה קְבוּרַת אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן –
— And when Abraham our father saw that Adam the First was buried there—
וּבֶאֱמֶת מִקּוֹדֶם הָיָה מִשְׁכַּן אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן בְּגַן עֵדֶן, שֶׁהָיָה מְלוּבָּשׁ בְּגוּף מְזוּכָּךְ, וְשָׁם הָיָה הַשְׁרָאַת הַשְּׁכִינָה;
— for originally Adam dwelt in Gan Eden clothed in a luminous body where the Shechinah rested;
וְאַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל כְּתִיב: "מְשַׁנֶּה פָנָיו וַתְּשַׁלְּחֵהוּ" (אִיּוֹב יד, כ),
— and after the sin it is written: "You change his countenance and send him away",
וְנִשְׁאַר הַגַּן עֵדֶן מִשְׁכַּן הַנְּשָׁמוֹת,
— Gan Eden remaining the spiritual abode of disembodied souls,
וְהַיְינוּ דְּשָׁם מִתְלַבְּשִׁים הַנְּשָׁמוֹת בְּגוּף מְזוּכָּךְ, כָּתְנוֹת אוֹר, כְּמוֹ אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל.
— where souls are enclothed in luminous garments of light (kotnot ohr / כותנות אור), like Adam before the sin.
וְאִיתָא בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה (בַּמִּדְבָּר פָּרָשָׁה ד, ח): "לָבַשׁ בִּגְדֵי כְּהֻנָּה גְּדוֹלָה וְכוּלֵי, בִּגְדֵי שַׁבָּת הָיוּ וְכוּלֵי",
— And it is taught in Midrash Rabbah (Bamidbar 4:8): Adam wore the vestments of the High Priesthood, which were the garments of Shabbat;
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאַף לְאַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל שֶׁנִּתְלַבֵּשׁ בְּמַשְׁכָּא דְּחִוְיָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ,
— meaning that even after the Fall, when mankind was clothed in coarse skins of the serpent (kotnot or / כותנות עור),
מִכָּל מָקוֹם בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ וּבְשַׁבָּת זוֹכִין לְכָתְנוֹת אוֹר כְּמוֹ אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל,
— nonetheless in the Holy Temple and on Shabbat we merit garments of light (kotnot ohr) like Adam before the Fall,
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה כ, יב): "בְּתוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר מָצְאוּ כָּתוּב: כָּתְנוֹת אוֹר (בְּאָלֶ"ף)".
— which is why in the scroll of Rabbi Meir they found written: "garments of light (ohr with an Alef)".
וְכֵן זָכָה לָזֶה אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן בִּמְעָרַת הַמַּכְפֵּלָה,
— And this radiance was sealed with Adam in the Cave of Machpelah,
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהָיָה מָקוֹם מְקוּדָּשׁ – קְנָאוֹ גַּם כֵּן בְּדָמִים.
— and because it was the holy gateway to Eden, Abraham purchased it with full silver.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 20:12: “‘The Lord God made for Adam and for his wife garments of hide (or), and clothed them’ (Genesis 3:21). In Rabbi Meir’s Torah, they found that ‘garments of or’ was written. These are the garments of Adam the first man, that were similar to the common rue, broad at the bottom and narrow at the top. Rabbi Yitzḥak Ravya says: They were as smooth as a fingernail and as pretty as jewels. Rabbi Yitzḥak said: It was like the thin linen garments that come from Beit She’an. (And they were called) garments of hide because they adhered to the skin. Rabbi Elazar said: Goat hides. Rabbi Aivu said: Garments that cover the skin. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: Hare hides. Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said: Hides with their wool. Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: Radiant hides. And the firstborn sons would use them. Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman said: They were camel wool and hare wool. (And they were called) ‘garments of hide’ because they were garments that come from hide. Rabbi Levi said: The Torah teaches you proper conduct: Eat according to your means, wear clothing that is less than your means, and dwell in a place that is more than your means. Eat according to your means – ‘From every tree of the garden you may eat’ (Genesis 2:16). Wear clothing that is less than your means –‘The Lord God made for Adam and for his wife (garments of hide).’ And dwell in a place that is more than your means – as two people resided in the entire world.”

p: וְכֵן יַעֲקֹב שֶׁבָּא לִשְׁכֶם בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת וְקָבַע שָׁם קְדוּשַׁת שַׁבָּת כָּאָמוּר,
— And likewise Jacob, arriving at Shechem on Friday evening and anchoring the sanctity of Shabbat there,
וְכָאן קָבַע גַּם כֵּן מָקוֹם לַה', וּכְמָה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיַּצֶּב שָׁם מִזְבֵּחַ וַיִּקְרָא לוֹ אֵל אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל" (שָׁם לג, כ) – קְנָאוֹ גַּם כֵּן בְּדָמִים.
— consecrating an altar unto Hashem, likewise bought the parcel of land with money.
וּקְרָאוֹ בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה "קְבוּרָתוֹ שֶׁל יוֹסֵף",
— And the Midrash designated Shechem as "the burial place of Joseph",
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה אַחַר שֶׁנּוֹלַד יוֹסֵף שִׂטְנוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגֶד קְלִיפַּת עֲמָלֵק.
— because this purchase transpired after the birth of Joseph, the adversary of Esau and Amalek.
דְּיוֹסֵף מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת צַדִּיק,
— For Joseph is the chariot for the attribute of Tzaddik (Yesod),
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהֵם קְשׁוּרִים בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
— signifying that the souls of Israel are bound in their essential root to Hashem,
וְלָכֵן מִזַּרְעוֹ יְכוֹלִים לִכְבּוֹשׁ עֲמָלֵק "רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם", כִּתְרִין דִּמְסָאֲבוּתָא.
— wherefore from his seed emerges the power to vanquish Amalek, the head of the impure crowns.
וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרָאִים עַל שְׁמוֹ: "שְׁאֵרִית יוֹסֵף" (עָמוֹס ה, טו).
— And all Israel are called by his name: "the remnant of Joseph" (Amos 5:15).
וְכָאן בִּשְׁכֶם, שֶׁהָיָה מָקוֹם מוּכָן לִשְׁלֹשָׁה קְלִיפּוֹת: הַקִּנְאָה, וְהַתַּאֲוָה, וְהַכָּבוֹד,
— And here in Shechem, which was primed for the three unholy husks of envy, lust, and honor,
קָבַע יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הַקְּדוּשָּׁה שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְהַכְנִיעָם,
— Jacob established the sanctity enabling Israel to subdue them,
וְהוּא עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ יוֹסֵף, שֶׁהוּא מְבָרֵר אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים":
— through the power of Joseph, who clarifies Israel to the stature of "Your people are all righteous":

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Kli Yakar, Bereishis 33:19: “‘He bought the parcel of the field’ – because he wanted to build an altar there, he did not want to offer burnt-offerings to Hashem for nothing, as David did at the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite (II Samuel 24:24). Scripture tells us that he bought it for a hundred kesitah, corresponding to the altar of the eternal House, whose height was a hundred cubits, in order to atone for every sin that flows from the sin of Adam. Adam was created stretching from one end of the heavens to the other, was diminished through his sin, and was reduced to a hundred cubits. Therefore the Sanctuary was a hundred cubits high, for man was formed from that place, of which it is said, ‘An altar of earth you shall make for Me,’ since the earth itself was also a cause of the sin.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Kli Yakar reads the purchase at Shechem as Rav Tzadok does: a place set aside for Hashem through an altar may not be taken for nothing, as David said to Araunah. He adds that the price of a hundred kesitah corresponds to the hundred-cubit Sanctuary, tying the purchase to the repair of Adam’s sin, which this os approaches through the Cave of Machpelah.

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 79:7: “… ‘He purchased the tract of the field where he had pitched his tent…for one hundred kesita’ – Rabbi Yudan bar Simon said: This is one of three places that the nations of the world cannot deride Israel and say: ‘They are stolen (property) in your hands,’ and these are: The Cave of Makhpela, the Temple, and Joseph’s tomb. The Cave of Makhpela, as it is written: ‘Abraham heeded Efron, and Abraham weighed for Efron (the money…)’ (Genesis 23:16). The Temple, as it is written: ‘David gave to Ornan for the place (six hundred shekels worth of gold)’ (I Chronicles 21:25). Joseph’s tomb – ‘he purchased the tract of the field’ (Genesis 33:19); Jacob purchased Shekhem. Rabbi Ḥiyya Rabba, Rabbi Shimon bar Rabbi, and Rabbi Shimon bar Ḥalafta forgot words from the Targum, and they came to a certain Arabian merchant to learn it from there. …”
